title: RAW_UNSCREENED: Graftkompatibilität als gerichteter Donor-Stock-Graph
summary: RAW_UNSCREENED: Columella/Palladius describe ordered graft relations with three insertion methods, stock-donor compatibility and altered fruit traits; the bound f57v four-near/four-between layout could encode transformations rather than two independent label lists.

design.scope_description: Nur die bereits gebundene f57v-Visualbeschreibung mit vier figurnahen und vier Zwischenfigurtexten sowie der zugängliche antike/lateinische Grafting-Vergleich; keine neue Bildauswertung.
design.mechanism: Each endpoint is a host or donor plant state; an intervening item records a directed graft method or compatibility relation, and the next endpoint records the inherited or altered product trait.
design.unit: The four cyclic endpoint inscriptions and four interfigure inscriptions recorded in the existing f57v source-bound report.
design.contrast: Gerichteter Donor-Stock- und Ergebnisgraph versus zwei parallele räumliche Beschriftungsregister.
design.prediction: A graft graph predicts that reversing an endpoint pair changes the legal relation or result, and that repeated host/donor classes reuse one of the three method families. The parallel-list model predicts no direction-sensitive bridge and allows the gap texts to vary independently of endpoint pairs.
concrete_observations: RAW_P30/GDT389 records four short f57v inscriptions near figures and four additional inscriptions between consecutive figures, with no drawn leader or bracket assigning a nearby item to one figure.

Columella, De Arboribus 26.1.1 explicitly distinguishes three methods: a split stock receiving scions, insertion between bark and wood, and budding under bark; it also states season and bark/fruit similarity constraints.

Palladius, De insitione 34-39 gives the same three-way technique inventory and then lists directed tree pairings whose graft changes fruit colour, size, flesh or thorniness; some trees exchange their own buds rather than accept an alien one.
linked_consequences: A source-like f57v reading requires every bridge to carry both an ordered endpoint pair and one method/compatibility class; a reverse pair cannot silently preserve the same relation.

It predicts a constrained output change at the following endpoint (for example colour, size, protection or fertility), while a bridge between incompatible endpoint classes should be exceptional or marked as failed.
The parallel-register rival predicts no systematic co-variation between endpoint pair order, intervening inscription and downstream endpoint, even if all eight items form a neat circle.
design.nearest_rival: Two independent cyclic lists placed together, with proximity and cyclic adjacency serving layout only; a repeated gap form is a reusable label rather than a donor-stock operation.
design.distinguishing_observation: Freeze the four endpoint pairs in their recorded cyclic order and compare exact intervening forms across repeated or reversed pair classes. A positive result needs direction-sensitive bridge reuse plus an endpoint change; adjacency alone is not evidence.
assumption_costs: The f57v four-plus-four grouping is source-bound and semantically co-owned.
A plant-transformation system can be represented without visible plant names or confirmed Voynich lexemes.
The historical three-method inventory is an analogue, not a licence to assign graft words.
design.strongest_likely_failure: f57v has no visible leaders and only four pairs; apparent endpoint-dependent bridges may be circular layout coincidence, leaving this stronger graph model indistinguishable from P30's independent-register rival.

primary_sources.source_consequence: Three methods, compatibility conditions and seasonal distinctions are written explicitly; method is separate from host/donor names.
Directed pairings produce altered fruit traits and include a non-accepting/self-exchanging exception.
